title: Additivity of a Fourier character on $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$
statement:
Fix integers $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$, let $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$, and for $s \in (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n$ let $\chi_s : (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be the character $\chi_s(x) = \omega_k^{\,s\cdot x}$, where $s\cdot x = \sum_{i=1}^{n} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ is the componentwise dot product. Then for all $x, y \in (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n$,
\[
\chi_s(x + y) = \chi_s(x)\,\chi_s(y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: k is a positive integer (NeZero k)
s is a fixed vector in (Z/kZ)^n
x and y are arbitrary vectors in (Z/kZ)^n
replaced:
For $s, x, y \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
$\chi_s(x + y) = \chi_s(x) \cdot \chi_s(y)$.
Each character is a group homomorphism from $(\mathbb{Z}_k^n, +)$ to
$(\mathbb{C}^\times, \cdot)$.
